title: Điểm gặp ở đâu?
summary: Ask "Where is the meeting point?" with Điểm gặp ở đâu?, then use the notes below to understand likely replies and next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: For travelers, Điểm gặp ở đâu? is the phrase to keep ready for "Where is the meeting point" in tickets, tours, photos, closing times, and meeting points. This comes before a tour, boat, or day trip starts. This avoids missed tours and pickup confusion. It works best when you focus on turning the problem into something the other person can point to, type, or mark on a map. After you say it, listen for a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name; the next rows help you keep the exchange moving.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern asks where a place or service is. Swap the first part to ask about another nearby stop.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Điểm gặp ở đâu? as your first sentence for "Where is the meeting point". This comes before a tour, boat, or day trip starts. Leave a short pause after the phrase so the other person can answer with a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name. Keep the booking, ticket, room number, or time visible when the exact detail matters.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Sightseeing phrases help staff answer with a point, ticket, time, or location. For "Where is the meeting point", Điểm gặp ở đâu? helps by turning the problem into something the other person can point to, type, or mark on a map. If the answer is longer than a point or a place name, ask them to show it on your phone.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In Sightseeing & Activities, the reply often comes as a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name. Say Điểm gặp ở đâu? once, pause, and watch for the reply before adding another sentence. Keep the booking, ticket, room number, or time visible when the exact detail matters.
